ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and hand signing authorities against: (i) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Government of Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List pursuant to the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; (iv) the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 8; and (v) applicable provincial securities cease-trade registries. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including domestic, foreign and international organization PEPs and their family/close associates, with documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification under PCMLTFA obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (BC Corporate Online)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters; non-Latin character sequences are not accepted. Names may be in English, French, or a combination, and must include a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Limited', etc.). If a name uses a word derived from a non-English or non-French language, an English or French translation may be required to permit a distinctiveness assessment under ss. 296–298 of the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, and the Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 289/2004.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant (or incorporator's lawyer) may file a written request for reconsideration with the Director of BC Registries within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching a revised name search report and any ministerial consents required. If the Director upholds the refusal, a new name reservation application may be filed, and the applicant may additionally seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. All submissions should be made through BC Corporate Online with proof of service and consents from affected regulatory bodies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for the registered office of a PropTech SaaS entity, provided the address is a physical street address in British Columbia where process may be served and documents are received during business hours; a post-office-box-only address is not acceptable. Practical risk is elevated because CRA and FINTRAC may assess commercial substance, so virtual-office arrangements should be supported by a local mail-and-scan agreement and be distinguished from the registered records office requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated under 5% unannounced on-site inspection risk in the first 12 months for this low-risk SaaS line, but potentially 15–20% if GST/HST input credits, payroll remittances, or Canadian-sourced revenue are material without commensurate physical substance; inspection triggers include unusual PEP flags, name-match sanctions hits, or bank referral.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (British Columbia), as amended; incorporation: s. 10 (Incorporation Application), s. 12 (Certificate of Incorporation); corporate name: ss. 21-24; authorized share structure and share issue: ss. 35, 51-58; directors: ss. 102, 110, 119-120; registered office and records office: ss. 198-201.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry Branch, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia; Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1 under the BC Business Corporations Act) together with Articles, Notice of Registered Office and Records Office, and Notice of Directors (Initial).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; shares may be issued without par value and consideration may consist of money, property, or past services. No escrow or capital deposit account is mandated for standard technology incorporation under the BCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for the initial issuance of common shares, as recorded in the share register, is approved and the shares are issued to the subscriber for payment in full of stated capital. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [address], British Columbia, with the records office maintained there. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the directors named in the Notice of Directors are duly elected, and the officers—President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer—are appointed to serve until the next annual general meeting. AND FURTHER RESOLVED, that the filed Articles are ratified, and the Directors are authorized to execute banking resolutions, CRA registrations, and ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry – Name Request service completed online through OneStart BC Business Registry (usually via a BCeID account).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online Name Request naming the proposed corporation (e.g., 'XYZ PropTech Solutions Inc.'); the Registry screens against the corporate name register and issues a Name Reservation valid for 56 days. If using a numerical designation or keywords such as 'real estate' or 'property management', ensure the name is not misleading under the BC business name regulation.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Request application
Proposed name and alternative names in priority order
Written consent from any third party whose name is used (if applicable)
Payment of CAD $30 name request fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the registrant may submit a revised application citing the registrar's objection reasons, or file a new Name Request with a distinct corporate name; no filing fee is forfeited for the incorporation application itself unless a certificate has already been issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Statutory Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and initial directors (preparatory act); documents subsequently remitted to the BC Corporate Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Application, specimen or special Articles, Notice of Registered Office and Records Office, and Notice of Directors. Each director must complete a signed Consent to Act as Director. The incorporation address must be a physical street address in British Columbia; a post-office box is not sufficient for the records office.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Incorporation Application
Articles of Incorporation (authorized share structure and special provisions)
Notice of Registered Office and Records Office (street address in BC)
Notice of Directors (initial directors' names, addresses)
Signed Consents to Act as Director
Name Reservation certificate or approved name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any deficiencies identified by legal review or the Registry (e.g., invalid director consents, unreserved names, incomplete share provisions) and re-execute; no resubmission fee is charged for correction within the same application window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application and Pay Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Branch, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online platform).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed incorporation package electronically through the Corporate Online service (or by paper with priority 'Registry Document Filing') and pay the CAD $250 basic incorporation fee (plus name request fee if not already paid). The Registrar will review the filing against the BCA and issue the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of Form 1 and Articles
Notice of Registered Office and Records Office
Notice of Directors
Payment confirmation (Corporate Online receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the filer receives an error notice with specific rejections; the filer may cure and resubmit the corrected record within the same business day via Corporate Online without losing name priority if the reservation remains valid. If the name reservation lapses, renew or replace it before final resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and CRA / PST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration; BC Ministry of Finance for PST registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the First Board Meeting to adopt the pro-forma resolution (share issuance, registered office confirmation, officer appointments), set up the minute book and share certificate records, and complete the CRA RC1 registration for a Business Number, GST/HST account (small supplier threshold or voluntary registration), BC PST account, and payroll deduction account if staffing begins. The board should also adopt the resolution to accept records office location and authorize bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Minute book and share register ledger
CRA RC1 – Request for a Business Number and accounts
Bank account opening package signed by officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA may return the RC1 for clarification of business activity or account registration dates; the company should promptly refile with corrected NAICS code 531390 / ISIC 6201 and confirm the GST/HST effective date. Any resulting late-filing penalties can be nullified by demonstrating good-faith correction within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and WorkSafeBC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver (or applicable BC municipality) Licensing Department; WorkSafeBC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal Business Licence for the registered office, selecting the classification for software / property-management technology services; register with WorkSafeBC for general employer coverage or confirm provincial workers' compensation classification; obtain a fire inspection and occupancy clearance certificate from the landlord or municipal fire marshal before employees use the premises.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Lease agreement or proof of office address
Fire safety / occupancy inspection report
WorkSafeBC firm registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a deficiency notice, pay any pro-rated licence fee, provide a revised floor plan or occupancy load calculation, and request re-inspection; WorkSafeBC registration can be backdated and amended by filing a corrected classification submission with the Employer Service Centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Privacy, Data-Protocol and E-Commerce Readiness Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of British Columbia (OIPC); Industry Canada / CRA for e-commerce and anti-spam (CASL) compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a privacy management program under the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), designate a privacy officer, execute data-processing schedules with Stripe Billing and ACH Direct payment rails, and post the required collection, use and disclosure notices for PropTech data. If the company sends commercial electronic messages (CEM) for tenant screening services, register a CASL-compliant unsubscribe protocol.
required_dossiers: PIPA privacy policy and consent forms
Privacy officer appointment resolution
Data processing addendum (with processors outside Canada)
CASL / CEM consent and unsubscribe templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: OIPC may request amendments to consent language or cross-border transfer disclosures; the company must file a revised policy with the OIPC contact and confirm the correction to ensure compliance before the anticipated authorized-institution launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure software / PropTech business; the relevant administrative bodies for ancillary physical premises are the BC Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation (sector support and trade licensing), the local municipal licensing department, and Technical Safety BC for regulated electrical/gas systems in leased office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit is mandated for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390 SaaS services; a municipal Business Licence (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence) is required for the office footprint.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based SaaS and PropTech data platform; no Environmental Assessment Certificate required under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 51, and no waste or effluent discharge permit is required under the Environmental Management Act, S.B.C. 2003, c. 53.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the software operation itself: the platform produces no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. For any subsequently acquired hardware or data centers, the company must comply with the BC Recycling Regulation for e-waste, the provincial municipal wastewater regulation if a physical office is later converted to light industrial use, and Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 standards for electronics disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance for the employee office; municipal fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code Division B (office occupancy); building occupancy and structural load inspection certificate issued by the local building authority; and, where payroll employees are based in BC, a WorkSafeBC employer registration number must be in effect before the first employee begins work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — via Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A British Columbia business corporation obtains a federal Business Number (BN) by registering with the CRA, either automatically upon federal incorporation or through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1 for a provincial/BC extraprovincial registration. The BN is a 9-digit taxpayer identifier and must be activated with separate program accounts for GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), corporate income tax (RC), and import/export (RM) as applicable. A foreign non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must register for a BN through a Canadian representative and provide the BC extraprovincial registration certificate or proof of place of business in Canada; the CRA must be notified of the non-resident's agent for service in Canada. No capital assessment or minimum capital filing requirement applies for registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists for a Canadian business corporation; a Canadian corporation is an opaque taxpayer and is taxed separately from its shareholders. The Income Tax Act nonetheless provides specified tax elections, including the s. 85 rollover for transfers of property to a corporation, s. 86 share-for-share exchange, s. 88 amalgamation/winding-up rollover, and certain deemed-dividend elections. Canada also applies hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 18.4–18.6) which can deny deductions for payments involving hybrid entities or conduit checks, including transactional structures that exploit classification mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; British Columbia also levies a separate Provincial Sales Tax (PST) generally not applicable to remote-access SaaS subscriptions
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) in any single calendar quarter for GST/HST registration; BC PST registration is required without a small-supplier threshold once taxable sales are made in BC, but remote SaaS is not subject to PST unless the customer takes possession/copies of software.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory government API e-invoicing. Electronic invoices are accepted if they meet the CRA's prescribed GST/HST invoice content requirements (supplier name and BN, recipient's GST/HST registration number where applicable, date, nature of supply, total consideration, and tax amount). The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Trust Framework and PEPPOL-based interoperability are voluntary and still in pilot stage; the CRA expects registered suppliers to maintain auditable digital records for electronic filing of GST/HST returns and to support CRA e-audit access.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Canadian SaaS supplier may zero-rate the supply of intangible personal property or services if the recipient is a non-resident person, the recipient is not registered for GST/HST, and the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or goods ordinarily situated in Canada. For PropTech SaaS used by a non-resident property manager outside Canada, the export supply is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act. If the cloud services are used to manage Canadian rental properties, zero-rating is unavailable and GST/HST at 5% applies. The supplier must evidence the non-resident status of the customer and the foreign use/consumption of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CERS export declaration / CBSA Form B13A (where physical goods or tangible software media are exported)
Commercial invoice and executed SaaS/property-management subscription contract
Bill of lading, air waybill or electronic delivery log (for goods) or remote server access/use evidence (for services)
SWIFT MT103 or bank remittance credit advice showing payment from the non-resident account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may deny zero-rating on audit where the documentary chain is incomplete, reassess the taxpayer within the four-year normal reassessment period, and, in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful evasion, reassess beyond the four-year limitation period without time bar. The resulting clawback includes unremitted GST/HST, daily compound interest, and penalties. A gross-negligence penalty of up to 50% of the tax amount or false credit claimed under the Excise Tax Act can be imposed, and criminal tax-evasion prosecution may lead to fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment. Fact patterns indicating sham export documentation will be escalated to criminal investigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary authority; foreign exchange supervision is exercised jointly by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential matters, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF and cross-border wire reporting, and Global Affairs Canada for economic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the United Nations Act. Canada has no dedicated exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. No exchange controls, prior approval, or repatriation licences apply to foreign direct investment, dividends, interest, management fees, or proceeds of a capital reduction. Profit remittance is subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5% for substantial-shareholder dividends under the Canada-US treaty and 15% for portfolio dividends). Capital returns on share redemption are not subject to withholding provided the paid-up capital is accurately maintained. Practical impediments are limited to sanctions screening, FINTRAC reporting of international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and verification that the beneficial owner is not a politically exposed person or sanctioned entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Canada. A Canadian exporter may retain foreign currency indefinitely in a domestic foreign-currency account or an offshore account. Reporting obligations under the CBSA B13A Export Declaration and Statistics Canada international merchandise trade program are statistical and customs-related only and do not require FX conversion or central bank approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with US Dollar Sweep

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a supplementary operational and receivables rail; Low as the sole treasury or capital-escrow vehicle. Canada does not issue an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence. Cross-border fintech platforms (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Legal constraints: no CDIC deposit insurance, funds are not treated as bank deposits, counterparty and single-platform concentration risk, and platform terms may restrict transactions involving rental-screening data or tenant payment processing. Use of an MSB is acceptable for sub-CAD 50,000 monthly US-dollar receivables from Stripe Billing and ACH Direct, but all capital injections, escrowed funds, and material trade disbursements must clear through a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement exists under the Bank Act or the Proceeds of Crime Regulations requiring directors to appear physically at a Canadian branch. All major Schedule I banks permit fully remote onboarding for a BC-registered corporation, subject to video-verified identification, notarized director affidavits, and a recorded compliance interview. Non-resident directors can satisfy KYC through apostilled or notarized passports, proof of residential address, and a bank reference letter from their home institution. In practice, certain regional credit unions (including Vancity) may require an in-person interview with a Canadian-resident director or locally appointed signing officer. That requirement is satisfied by appointing a BC-incorporated corporate services provider or a local law firm as an additional authorized signatory; the non-resident director need not travel to Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and shareholders with no Canadian operating footprint or physical office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and proof of address for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; BC Corporate Online registry excerpt showing active and in-good-standing status; certificate of incumbency; board resolution authorizing account opening; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; CRA Business Number confirmation; organizational chart illustrating the ownership chain; bank references from the shareholder's home institution; and a three-year projected transaction-volume statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech activities mischaracterized as real estate brokerage or property management, triggering trust-account and licensing expectations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A legal opinion distinguishing the SaaS model from property management under the BC Real Estate Services Act; executed SaaS terms of service demonstrating no legal custody, control, or disbursement of tenant funds; privacy impact assessment under BC PIPA and Canadian PIPEDA; and software licence agreements showing the tenant-screening analytics product as the sole deliverable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume US ACH and Stripe Billing settlement from US-based landlord/tenant counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe and ACH gateway agreements; PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance; sample invoices and merchant statements; a documented reconciliation procedure between settlement reports and bank statements; W-8BEN-E confirming Canadian tax residence for US withholding purposes; and a written explanation of expected monthly settlement volume and currency conversion requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP exposure arising from tenant-screening data of foreign nationals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Details of the automated SEMA/OFAC/UN sanctions screening protocol; PEP risk rating methodology; a written client-restriction policy excluding sanctioned jurisdictions; designation of a compliance officer; and evidence that no payments are routed to or from comprehensively sanctioned countries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent non-resident shareholder loans creating thin capitalization or deemed-benefit audit risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan agreements; CRA prescribed interest-rate calculation for the relevant tax quarters; board resolutions approving each loan; consolidated financial statements; and a debt-to-equity worksheet demonstrating compliance with the 1.5:1 disproportionate debt-to-equity threshold under section 18(4)-(6) of the Income Tax Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections and shareholder subordinated loans should be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pacs.008) to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account at a Schedule I bank. The remittance instruction must include the bank-specific Balance of Payments purpose code in SWIFT field 70, selecting 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' or 'Direct Investment - Intercompany Debt' as applicable. Supporting documents on file must include the executed share subscription or loan agreement, directors' resolution, inward remittance advice, and a legal entity identifier. No exchange-control approval is required. CAD funds settle over the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); USD funds clear via Fedwire through the Canadian bank's US correspondent. For BC regulatory clarity, the subscription price must be credited to the escrow account and later transferred to the operating account only upon issuance of shares under the BC Business Corporations Act. Subsequent capital reductions follow the same reverse rail, subject to the statutory solvency test.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operating disbursements for SaaS licensing, cloud infrastructure, subcontractors, and marketing vendors should be executed through SWIFT MT103 (or pacs.008) for CAD/USD cross-border payments; US-dollar ACH origination through the bank's US clearing partner for recurring lower-value payments; and commercial documentary credits (SWIFT MT700) for material vendor contracts requiring security under Incoterms 2020. CAD settlement is cleared via LVTS or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS); USD settlement clears via Fedwire/CHIPS through the Canadian bank's US correspondent. FINTRAC reporting applies to international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, to be filed within five business days. Beneficiary bank-account validation and name screening must be completed before release to mitigate sanctions and fraud risk. Dual-currency accounts at the same institution allow same-day natural treasury offset without crossing FX spreads.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable vanilla CAD/USD foreign exchange forwards (spot-deferred and fixed-date)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for tenant-payment currencies without deep offshore liquidity (e.g., emerging-market currencies)
Cross-currency swaps and coupon exchanges between CAD and USD
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures on regulated North American exchanges
Vanilla FX options, zero-cost collars, and knock-in/knock-out structures documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Schedule I Canadian bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: British Columbia Annual Report (including confirmation of Beneficial Ownership / Transparency Register information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Registry, Government of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation, or of extraprovincial registration in British Columbia, per the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 500 (approximately USD 370) once the report is overdue; annual report omission for two consecutive years permits administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar after final notice; restoration requires an order of the Registrar or the court plus payment of all arrears and any applicable penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act — required only if the entity is incorporated federally under the CBCA and is also registered extraprovincially in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within sixty days after the anniversary date of incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No graduated late fee; failure to file the annual return for two consecutive years authorizes the Director of Corporations to dissolve the corporation; reinstatement requires an application for revival to Corporations Canada or a court order together with all outstanding filing fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and accompanying financial statements (federal and British Columbia corporate income tax administered by the Canada Revenue Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year; balance-due day is three months after year end for Canadian-controlled private corporations and two months for non-CCPC corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, doubled for repeated failures; statutory daily compound arrears interest on unpaid balances; persistent non-filing may result in tax prosecution and CRA-initiated registration enforcement actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act and the Canada Business Corporations Act, an independent statutory audit is mandatory only for distributing (public) corporations. A private, non-distributing corporation has no compulsory audit solely by revenue or asset threshold; it may waive the audit by unanimous shareholder resolution or unanimous written consent. Shareholders holding 5% or more of the issued voting shares may requisition an audit, and lender or investor covenants may independently require one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private enterprises, as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook; the T2 tax return is reconciled to taxable income under the Income Tax Act from the chosen GAAP basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia companies must maintain a current Transparency Register of every individual with significant control (ISC), defined as direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of voting shares, control of 25% or more of votes, or the right to elect or remove a majority of directors. Any share transfer that changes significant control must be recorded in the register immediately upon knowledge and is confirmed to the Registrar as part of the BC Annual Report. For CBCA federal corporations, a Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be maintained and ISC information is reported with the federal annual return; companies must respond to ISC disclosure requests within 10 days and individuals within 15 days of a request. Annual confirmation is embedded in the annual report filing, not a separate standalone return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholder and director meetings and written resolutions)
Beneficial Ownership / Transparency Register (Individuals with Significant Control)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 to 450 per year (CAD 160 to 600), depending on provincial-only versus federal-plus-British Columbia service levels and corporate agent support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 to 20,000 (CAD 11,000 to 27,000) for a full statutory audit; USD 3,000 to 5,000 (CAD 4,000 to 7,000) for a review engagement when the unanimous audit waiver is applicable
